opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Finding and testing new medicines — 17% of revenue.

opex.name: Marketing, selling & administrative
opex.note: Sales teams and launch campaigns for new medicines, up 25%.

opex.name: Acquired IPR&D
opex.note: Research bought with acquisitions — mainly Orna Therapeutics and Ajax Therapeutics, expensed on day one.

opex.name: Asset impairment & restructuring
opex.note: Charges tied to closing the Kelonia and Centessa acquisitions, including faster vesting of employee stock awards.

follow100Note: Two shots — Mounjaro and Zepbound — brought in $64.73 of every $100. After production costs, the biggest single drag was $12.08 of research Lilly bought through acquisitions and expensed immediately. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Reported (GAAP) figures throughout; Lilly's non-GAAP net income was $7,493M (EPS $8.38).
oneTimers: Acquired IPR&D of $2,776M — research bought via the Orna Therapeutics and Ajax Therapeutics acquisitions, expensed immediately. It cost $3.03 of EPS; a year ago the same line was $154M.
Asset impairment, restructuring and other special charges of $703M, mostly accelerated vesting of employee stock awards and integration costs from closing the Kelonia and Centessa deals.
A $250M sales milestone for Jardiance, paid by partner Boehringer Ingelheim, sits inside 'All other medicines' revenue — a one-off boost to that line.
otherDetail: Net other income of $269M — interest costs of $274M more than covered by $543M of other income, including gains on equity investments.

segments.name: Mounjaro
segments.note: The diabetes and weight-loss shot (tirzepatide). U.S. sales were $4.8B (+45%); sales outside the U.S. more than doubled after Mounjaro joined China's reimbursement list.

segments.name: Zepbound
segments.note: The same drug sold for obesity in the U.S., Canada and Japan. U.S. sales rose 44% despite lower cash-pay prices.

segments.name: All other medicines
segments.note: Everything else — cancer, immunology and diabetes medicines such as Trulicity and Jardiance, including a $250M Jardiance milestone payment.

takeaways.text: Mounjaro revenue rose 91% to $9.9B and Zepbound 46% to $4.9B. Volume did the work: worldwide volume rose 60%, partly offset by realized prices 13% lower.
takeaways.title: Mounjaro nearly doubled

takeaways.text: Lilly booked $2.8B of acquired research charges (Orna, Ajax) plus $703M of deal-related impairment and restructuring. Excluding items like these, non-GAAP profit was $7.5B versus the reported $7.1B.
takeaways.title: Acquisition charges ate a chunk

takeaways.text: The effective tax rate rose to 23.3% from 16.5%, mainly because the acquired-research charges are not tax-deductible — one reason profit grew 25% while operating income grew 31%.
takeaways.title: The tax rate jumped

verdict: Lilly's revenue jumped 48% to $23.0B as Mounjaro sales nearly doubled to $9.9B — and even after $3.5B of acquisition-related charges, it kept $7.1B as profit.
